scenes.narration: Epictetus opens his little handbook with one simple split.
Of things, some are in our power, and others are not.
Your opinions, intentions, desires and choices are yours to direct. Your body, possessions, reputation and job title can be influenced, but never fully controlled.
Most stress comes from treating the second group as if it belonged in the first: needing the promotion, the praise, the perfect outcome.

params.note: Effort here. Hold the rest loosely.

scenes.narration: So put your effort where your control is real, like preparation, honesty and how you respond, and hold everything else more loosely.
Take one worry and split it into two columns: what I control, and what I don't. Then act on one item from the first column today.
